newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed weaker but off their day's lows in a quiet market dominated by professional trading as institutions stayed on the sidelines.
Dealers said most activity was in German Bund futures with the U.S. election on Tuesday keep trading volumes low, despite the common view that Bill Clinton would retain the presidency.
"It's all pre-election quietness," said one trader.
One dealer said most losses were made at the opening, with prices edging up on squaring of long positions, adding that the short end bore the brunt of the weakness.
"For some reason, there's nervousness about the short end," said one trader, adding that longer maturities held up better.
He said recent Bundesbank comments that German interest rates would not be cut may have ignited fears they would rise.
Another dealer pointed to weakness in 2004 and 2007 paper today. "Maybe someone is trying to unwind their positions. There's no real cash buying," he said.
He said maturities between 1999 and 2004 were now proving difficult to sell. "If there's any demand, it's for the (January 2006 bond) or longer dated paper," he said.
